extraction.name: C-EVAL
extraction.description: C-EVAL is the first comprehensive Chinese evaluation suite designed to assess advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities of foundation models in a Chinese context. It comprises 13948 multiple-choice exam questions spanning 52 diverse disciplines, ranging from humanities to science and engineering, across four difficulty levels: middle school, high school, college, and professional. C-EVAL is accompanied by C-EVAL HARD, a subset of very challenging subjects that requires advanced reasoning abilities.
extraction.creator: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Tsinghua University, University of Edinburgh, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
extraction.citeAs: Huang, Y., Bai, Y., Zhu, Z., Zhang, J., Zhang, J., Su, T., Liu, J., Lv, C., Zhang, Y., Lei, J., Fu, Y., Sun, M., He, J. C-EVAL: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models. NeurIPS 2023.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data were collected from mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top universities in China publicly shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam sourced from the Weipu website (with authorization for around 2000 questions). Questions were collected as PDF or Microsoft Word documents and a minor fraction as web pages, then parsed automatically or manually into a structured format.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Mock exams freely available on the internet, past exam questions from top Chinese universities shared by students, and mock questions for the national graduate entrance exam from the Weipu website (https://kaoyan.cqvip.com/view/postgraduate/index.aspx).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All questions were processed to include exactly four choices. Questions with fewer than four options were eliminated, and for questions with more than four options, incorrect choices were randomly dropped. For subjects with complex mathematical notations (such as STEM subjects), notations were manually converted into standard LaTeX formats.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF documents were initially processed into text. Questions were parsed (automatically when possible, otherwise manually by the authors) into a structured format. Standard data preprocessing pipeline was followed, including deduplication and cleaning. Questions underwent several rounds of human validation by the authors, with LaTeX notations ensured to compile without syntax errors. Questions were randomly split into development (5 per subject), validation, and test splits (1:9 ratio between validation and test).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Development set exemplars (5 per subject) were annotated with explanations to enable few-shot chain-of-thought settings. Explanations were generated by first prompting GPT-4 to generate step-by-step explanation of the ground-truth answer, then manually revised by the authors to obtain the final explanations.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 (used to generate initial step-by-step explanations for dev set exemplars)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The labels of the test split are kept private. Users submit model predictions to https://cevalbenchmark.com to automatically obtain test accuracy, where a public leaderboard is maintained. Users can optionally include their submission results on the live leaderboard.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The authors hope C-EVAL will help analyze important strengths and shortcomings of foundation models, guide developers to understand the abilities of their models from multiple dimensions, and foster development and growth of foundation models for Chinese users.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that English benchmarks tend to exhibit geographical biases towards domestic knowledge of the regions that produce them. C-EVAL aims to address this by focusing on Chinese context knowledge.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: C-EVAL is limited to multiple-choice format questions. It is far from perfect for LLM evaluation as there are many other abilities (such as reasoning over and calling APIs) and aspects beyond accuracy (safety, bias, robustness) that are not covered. Potential data contamination risk exists due to online availability of similar questions, though efforts were made to mitigate this by collecting from mock exams rather than official national exams.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing/Evaluation of foundation models' advanced knowledge and reasoning abilities in a Chinese context. The dataset is split into development (few-shot exemplars), validation (hyperparameter tuning), and test sets. Evaluation is conducted in both zero-shot and five-shot settings, with both answer-only and chain-of-thought prompting.
